source.check: returned unopposed: no nomination was received for the division and the retiring member continued (Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3); named as a sitting member of the new council early in the term (Belfast News-Letter, 11 December 1946, p. 6: 'Captain H. Lecky, D.L., opposing, said that the Council had no jurisdiction' on rights of private ownership (the Giant's Causeway, Portrush area); 'Captain Lecky also mentioned the case of Carrick-a-Rede')

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received on 19 September 1946, withdrawals to 20 September, and the day of election was Thursday 3 October 1946 (official notice, Belfast News-Letter, 6 September 1946, p. 2). Polling took place on 3 October ('Polling took place ... yesterday', Belfast News-Letter, 4 October 1946, p. 3) and the count was held on 4 October. No party labels were printed. Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Portrush. division inferred from the 1 June 1939 return (Captain H. Leckey, D.L.; Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1939, p. 13); the Belfast News-Letter, 11 December 1946, p. 6 names the member as sitting for the new council (meeting of Antrim County Council, Tuesday 10 December 1946 (Bigger Belfast opposed; tourists and toll charges)). No nomination was received for Portrush in 1946, so the retiring member continued. The 1946 reports do not name him; he spoke as a member at the council's meeting of 10 December 1946, ten weeks after the election day. The first meeting (15 October 1946, Belfast News-Letter 16 October 1946, p. 3) is reported without a list of members. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
